metaTitle: Dubai to Abu Dhabi by Road: Route, Duration and Tolls
metaDescription: Dubai to Abu Dhabi by road is about 130 km and around 90 minutes. The E11 route, Salik and Darb tolls, what slows the drive and how a fixed-price car works.
excerpt: Dubai to Abu Dhabi by road takes around 90 minutes on Sheikh Zayed Road, with Salik and Darb tolls along the way. Here is the route, what changes the journey time, and how a fixed-price chauffeur transfer handles all of it.
quickAnswer: Dubai to Abu Dhabi by road is about 130 km, mostly on Sheikh Zayed Road (E11), and a private car does it in around 90 minutes door to door. You pass Salik gates in Dubai and Darb gates in Abu Dhabi, where the toll is AED 4 per pass at peak hours only. Weekday rush hours, winter fog and where in each city you start and finish stretch the time.
content:
Dubai to Abu Dhabi by road is about 130 km on a motorway, and a private car does it in around 90 minutes door to door. Sheikh Zayed Road (E11) carries you most of the way, and the time you actually spend in the seat depends on where in Dubai you start, when you leave and where in Abu Dhabi you finish. This guide walks the route, the tolls, the timings and the things that quietly add half an hour.

What does the Dubai to Abu Dhabi drive look like at a glance?

FactDetailSource
Main roadSheikh Zayed Road, the Dubai stretch of the E11, which the UAE government describes as the longest road in the country at around 553 kmUAE Government portal
Alternative roadSheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Road (E311), around 220 km end to end, running inland of the E11UAE Government portal
DistanceAbout 130 km from central Dubai to central Abu DhabiCommon route knowledge, varies by pickup and drop-off
Typical durationAround 90 minutes with clear traffic, longer at peak timesEmirates Limo chauffeur experience on the route
Dubai tollsSalik gates, charged to every vehicle including taxis, with a toll that varies by time of dayUAE Government portal
Abu Dhabi tollsDarb gates charge AED 4 per pass at peak hours only: 07:00 to 09:00 and 15:00 to 19:00, except Sundays and official holidaysAbu Dhabi Mobility
Emirates Limo pickupAny address in Dubai, 24 hours a day, fixed price at booking, 15 minutes free waiting at the doorEmirates Limo service terms

What should I have ready before the car arrives?

You need very little for this drive, but the small things decide whether the day runs smoothly. Have these sorted before your chauffeur pulls up.

  • The exact pickup address, with a building name or hotel entrance, not just a district
  • The exact drop-off in Abu Dhabi, including the tower, gate or hotel name
  • A pickup time that leaves a buffer for the traffic patterns described below
  • Your phone charged and WhatsApp on, so the chauffeur can reach you at the door
  • A child seat requested at booking if you are travelling with a small child
  • Passenger and luggage numbers matched to the right vehicle on the Emirates Limo fleet page
  • Your booking confirmation email, which arrives the moment payment goes through

Which road do you take from Dubai to Abu Dhabi?

Sheikh Zayed Road, the E11, is the road for almost every Dubai to Abu Dhabi trip. It runs straight down the coast past Dubai Marina, Jebel Ali and the border at Ghantoot, then becomes the main approach into the capital. The UAE Government portal lists the E11 as the country's longest road at roughly 553 km, stretching from the Saudi border to Ras Al Khaimah.

Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Road, the E311, is the sensible alternative if you start in Deira, Mirdif, Dubai Silicon Oasis or near Dubai International. It sits inland and joins the E11 well south of Jebel Ali, so it skips the busiest urban section of Sheikh Zayed Road. The same government page puts the E311 at around 220 km in total.

Your chauffeur picks between them on the day based on live traffic, not habit. From Downtown, the Marina or the Palm, the E11 wins nearly every time; from the airport side of the city, the E311 often shaves ten to fifteen minutes.

How long does Dubai to Abu Dhabi take by car?

Around 90 minutes is the honest answer for most trips, measured from the door in Dubai to the door in Abu Dhabi. Marina or Jebel Ali to the Corniche can be closer to 75 minutes with the road clear; Deira to Saadiyat Island or Yas Island can run past 100 minutes even on a good day.

The motorway section is fast and predictable because the speed limit is high and the road is wide. The time is lost at the two ends: getting out of Dubai's inner districts and getting across the bridges onto Abu Dhabi island.

If you have a meeting at 10:00 in Abu Dhabi, leaving Downtown Dubai at 08:00 works. Leaving at 08:30 is a gamble, and on a Monday it is a gamble you will lose.

Which tolls do you pass between Dubai and Abu Dhabi?

Two toll systems sit on this route: Salik in Dubai and Darb in Abu Dhabi. Both are fully electronic, so there are no barriers and no stopping, and with a chauffeur you never think about either because every toll is already inside the fixed price.

Salik gates sit on Sheikh Zayed Road and on a few other Dubai roads. The UAE Government portal states that every vehicle including taxis pays Salik when it passes a gate, and that the toll now varies with the time of passage. The RTA points drivers to the toll operator's own site for gate locations and current rates, from its Salik service page.

Darb is Abu Dhabi's system, run by Abu Dhabi Mobility. According to the official Darb fees page, the charge is AED 4 for each pass through a gate during peak hours, which are 07:00 to 09:00 and 15:00 to 19:00, except on Sundays and official holidays. Outside those windows, and all day on Sundays and public holidays, there is nothing to pay.

Abu Dhabi Mobility has also removed the daily and monthly caps on Darb, so a driver making repeated peak crossings pays for every one. For a single visit this changes nothing, but it is why an hourly booking with several stops on and off the island makes more sense with a fixed price than with a meter.

What affects the Dubai to Abu Dhabi journey time?

Time of day matters more than anything else. Weekday mornings between 07:00 and 09:00 push commuter traffic out of Dubai and into Abu Dhabi, and the reverse flow builds from 16:00 to 19:00. Those are the same hours Darb charges, which tells you the capital's own transport authority considers them the busy ones.

Where you start decides how much city driving comes before the motorway. Dubai Marina and Jebel Ali are practically already on the E11 heading south; Downtown adds ten minutes; Deira, Bur Dubai and the airport add twenty or more, unless the E311 is quiet.

Where you finish matters just as much. Yas Island and the airport area sit before the bridges, so they are quicker than the Corniche or Al Bateen at the far end of the island, and Saadiyat sits behind its own approach road from the Sheikh Khalifa Bridge side.

Weather is the wildcard. Fog on winter mornings, roughly December to February, brings visibility and speed limits down along the E11 and can add thirty minutes. Heavy rain, which is rare but not unheard of in the same months, does the same.

Roadworks and events round out the list. Race weekend on Yas, major concerts and big exhibitions at ADNEC fill the approaches into the city, and a chauffeur who drives the route daily knows which days to leave early.

How does an Emirates Limo Dubai to Abu Dhabi transfer work?

You book online, pick a vehicle, pay by card and get an emailed confirmation straight away. The price is fixed at the moment you book, so traffic, tolls and a slow crawl over the Maqta Bridge never change what you pay. A private car from Dubai to Abu Dhabi runs 24 hours a day, every day, including public holidays.

The chauffeur arrives at your door at the booked time and waits 15 minutes free of charge. Airport pickups are different: at DXB, DWC and AUH the chauffeur waits inside arrivals with a name board, the flight is tracked, and you get 60 minutes of free waiting counted from the actual landing time.

Cancellation is simple. Cancel 24 hours or more before pickup and you get a full refund; cancel inside 24 hours, or miss the pickup, and the booking is charged in full.

Which vehicle is right for the Dubai to Abu Dhabi run?

A sedan is right for up to three passengers with normal luggage, an SUV or van for families and groups. Every car in the fleet is chauffeur-driven, so the choice is about space and comfort, not about who is driving.

Ninety minutes is long enough that legroom counts. The S-Class and the 7-Series are the cars to choose when you want to answer emails and arrive fresh, and the V-Class is the one for a group that wants to talk on the way.

What goes wrong on Dubai to Abu Dhabi transfers?

The most common problem is a pickup time chosen for a clear road on a day that is not clear. Booking a 08:15 pickup from Deira for a 09:30 meeting on the Corniche leaves no margin, and the fix is to book 45 minutes earlier and use the spare time in the hotel lobby rather than in a queue on the Maqta Bridge.

The second is a vague address. "Marina" covers dozens of towers and "Yas" covers hotels, a circuit and a mall, so give the tower name and the entrance, and put a phone number the chauffeur can call on the booking.

Late changes are the third. A drop-off switched from Yas Island to Al Bateen while the car is already on the E11 adds real distance and time, so tell us on WhatsApp as early as you can and the chauffeur can re-route and the office can confirm any price difference before you set off.

Luggage that does not fit is the one that ruins a morning. Three large suitcases and two carry-ons will not go in a sedan, so match the numbers on the fleet page and go up a size if you are unsure.

Finally, forgetting the return. If you are coming back the same day, book the Abu Dhabi to Dubai transfer at the same time so the car is waiting, or book by the hour so the same chauffeur stays with you all day.

Can I go straight from Dubai airport to Abu Dhabi?

Yes, and it is one of the most common versions of this drive. From Dubai International the chauffeur takes the E311 or Al Khail Road to join the E11 south of the city, and from Al Maktoum you are already close to the motorway, so DWC to Abu Dhabi is the shorter run of the two.

An airport pickup works differently from a door pickup. Book a Dubai airport transfer with Abu Dhabi as the drop-off and the chauffeur meets you inside arrivals with a name board, the flight is tracked so a late landing moves the pickup automatically, and the first 60 minutes of waiting are free from the moment the aircraft lands.

Add the airport time to the drive when you plan. Immigration and baggage at DXB can take an hour on a busy evening, so a 20:00 landing means a realistic 22:30 arrival at an Abu Dhabi hotel, not 21:30.

Is a day trip better by the hour or as two transfers?

By the hour wins when you have more than one stop in Abu Dhabi. The hourly chauffeur service starts from AED 150 per hour, the car and driver stay with you for unlimited stops, and there is no second booking to think about for the way home.

Two transfers win when Abu Dhabi is one place for one purpose, such as a meeting, a wedding or a hotel stay, because you only pay for the two drives. For a mosque visit, lunch on Saadiyat and an afternoon at Yas, the hourly option is nearly always the calmer choice.

Whichever you choose, the same waiting and cancellation rules apply, and the details are on the Emirates Limo FAQ if you want them in writing.

faqs.question: How long does it take to drive from Dubai to Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Around 90 minutes door to door for a private car, over roughly 130 km of motorway. Starting from Dubai Marina or Jebel Ali can bring it closer to 75 minutes, while Deira to the Corniche or Saadiyat in weekday rush hour can pass 100 minutes.

faqs.question: Which road goes from Dubai to Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Sheikh Zayed Road, the E11, is the main road and runs down the coast through Jebel Ali and Ghantoot into Abu Dhabi. Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Road, the E311, is the inland alternative that suits pickups near Dubai International, Deira or Mirdif.

faqs.question: Are there tolls between Dubai and Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Yes. Salik gates on Dubai's roads charge every vehicle a toll that varies by time of day, and Abu Dhabi's Darb gates charge AED 4 per pass at peak hours, 07:00 to 09:00 and 15:00 to 19:00, except Sundays and official holidays. With Emirates Limo all tolls sit inside the fixed price.

faqs.question: What is the best time to leave Dubai for Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Leave before 07:00 or between 09:30 and 15:00 on a weekday for the clearest run. The 07:00 to 09:00 and 15:00 to 19:00 windows are commuter peaks in both directions and the same hours Abu Dhabi charges its Darb toll.

faqs.question: Can I book a car from Dubai to Abu Dhabi and back on the same day?
faqs.answer: Yes. Book two transfers if Abu Dhabi is a single stop, or book the hourly chauffeur service, from AED 150 per hour, if you have several stops, so the same car and driver stay with you all day. Cancel 24 hours or more before pickup for a full refund.
